subject: Re: Helios MSA - service-level commitments & evidence requirements
messages:
From: Clare Thomas <clare.thomas@helios.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helios.co
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helios MSA - proposed adjustments to service commitments

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the SLA section and flagged a few items that need clarification before procurement can sign: 

- Uptime target: our standard requires 99.99% for production endpoints that serve PHI-related inference. Can you confirm if Redwood will take that as-is or propose an alternate ramp?
- Service credits: need a clear formula (per-incident or monthly aggregate), with a reasonable monthly cap.
- Response times: we need P1 acknowledged within 30 minutes and mitigation plan within 2 hours; P2 within 4 hours.
- Maintenance windows: we can only accept a single scheduled maintenance window per calendar month, max 4 hours, with 72 hours notice and a blackout for major healthcare events.
- Evidence: procurement requires an evidence matrix listing artifacts Redwood will provide to validate availability/service credit triggers (uptime logs, KV-cache metrics, per-region incident timeline, raw request/response counters). Please include retention windows for those artifacts.

Please send your counterproposal on the SLA language and an evidence matrix. Procurement would also like to close legal redlines within 2 weeks; can you confirm a point of contact and timeline?

Regards,
Clare Thomas
Head of Procurement
Helios Health

Attachment: (none in this message)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Clare Thomas <clare.thomas@helios.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helios MSA - proposed adjustments to service commitments

Hi Clare —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a pragmatic counterproposal and an evidence matrix so we can close this quickly:

Key points we propose (high level):
- Uptime: 99.95% committed for year 1; 99.99% is something we can review at renewal once we have production telemetry. If you need 99.99% day-1 for specific PHI endpoints, we can explore a dedicated capacity/Private deployment option as a separate line item.
- Credits: credits are calculated monthly based on total query availability; formula attached in the matrix. Monthly credit cap proposal: 100% of one month of service for acute outage scenarios; otherwise stair-step credits for lower severities.
- Response SLA: propose P1 1 hour acknowledge / 4 hour mitigation window; P2 4 hour acknowledge / 24 hour mitigation. We can shorten for Dedicated customers.
- Maintenance: propose two tiers — a quarterly disruptive maintenance window (up to 4 hours) + monthly low-impact patching (up to 1 hour) with 48 hours notice. This preserves availability while reducing risk for broad blackouts.
- Evidence: attached SLA_evidence_matrix.xlsx maps the artifact, owner, retention, and granularity (per-region, per-model). We propose 12-month retention for forensic logs; longer retention available as an add-on.

I've attached the evidence matrix and a short redline summary. Laura and Markus are on this thread to help finalize legal and ops wording.

Next steps: 1) Laura to confirm operational cadence; 2) Markus to add legal-friendly language; 3) Ben to circulate a DocuSign-ready MSA after alignment. Can you share your target signing date and whether procurement needs a fully redlined PDF or an editable Word document?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- SLA_evidence_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- summary_sla_counterproposal.txt (plain text)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Clare Thomas <clare.thomas@helios.co>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helios MSA - proposed adjustments to service commitments

Hi Clare,

Operational note from our side to help procurement evaluate risk: 
- We can support a single monthly maintenance window up to 4 hours, but in practice many critical fixes require targeted hotfixes that are lower-impact — we propose documenting those as "low-impact patching" and counting them separately. This prevents stacking all work into one window and reduces emergency work.
- Notification: 48 hours for low-impact; 72 hours for disruptive quarterly windows. For PII/PHI-sensitive events we will also notify the primary account admin and the security contact.
- Evidence we can reasonably provide without compromising customer privacy: uptime graphs by region, per-route request counters, KV cache hit rates, and an incident timeline with root-cause analysis. For raw request logs we can provide aggregated counts; forensic-level request payloads require a narrower legal/data request.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week to align cadence and finalize the matrix. Proposed times: Fri 6/13 10–11am PT or Mon 6/16 9–11am PT.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Clare Thomas <clare.thomas@helios.co>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helios MSA - proposed adjustments to service commitments (legal redlines attached)

Clare, Ben —

I attached a legal redline (Helios_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf) with a few recommendations and questions for procurement: 

1) Audit/evidence scope: Helios requests a set of artifacts to trigger credits. We agree to provide uptime metrics, aggregated request counters, and incident timelines. However, any request for raw request/response payloads will need a separate, limited-scope forensic request (to preserve other customers' data). We propose adding language that defines the precise artifact set and a process to request additional artifacts.

2) Retention: we can commit to 12 months of forensic-level logs and 24 months of aggregated availability metrics. If Helios requires 24 months of raw forensic data, we need to scope storage and a pricing addendum.

3) Cap on credits and remedy limitation: raised a flag on unlimited monthly cap. Suggested language in the redline limits cumulative credits to a reasonable amount and preserves carveouts for state/local regulations.

4) Timezones and measurement: define UTC as the official clock for availability measurement and specify per-region SLA measurement windows. 

5) Phased commit: given Helios' PHI needs, I suggest a phased SLA commitment: commit to 99.95% for the first 12 months with a written checkpoint at month 9 to agree on adjustments. This mirrors Ben's operational recommendation and creates a path to 99.99% without blocking go-live.

Please confirm whether procurement wants the redline as a tracked Word document or a PDF comment set; once we have that, Ben can initiate DocuSign.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Helios_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf (annotated redline)

From: Clare Thomas <clare.thomas@helios.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helios.co, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helios MSA - service-level commitments & evidence requirements

Ben/Markus/Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the evidence matrix and legal redlines. A few confirmations from procurement: 

- Helios can accept the phased approach: 99.95% for year one with a documented checkpoint at month 9 and an option to move to 99.99% at renewal.
- For evidence, procurement will accept 12 months of forensic logs as long as Redwood confirms a secure transfer and limited-use agreement; however, we will request 24 months of aggregated availability metrics. Please include the transfer process in the evidence matrix.
- Service credits: procurement prefers a monthly aggregate formula rather than per-incident; the matrix looks reasonable but please ensure caps are clearly stated.
- Maintenance: Helios accepts the quarterly disruptive window + monthly low-impact patching model, provided we get 72 hours notice for disruptive events tied to major releases.

Procurement would like the final redline set in Word with tracked changes for our counsel to review. Can you produce that and send a DocuSign-ready version once both sides accept the tracked Word redline? Our target signing date is end of month (2025-06-30). We are available for a call Wed 6/18 at 10am PT to finalize any remaining items.

Action items for Redwood:
- Ben: circulate tracked Word redline as requested and include DocuSign link when ready.
- Markus: confirm retention/transfer language and add limited-use clause for forensic data.
- Laura: join the 6/18 call to finalize ops cadence.

Appreciate the collaboration — procurement is aligned to move quickly once the redline Word doc is produced.

Best,
Clare Thomas
Head of Procurement
Helios Health
